summary: Seven-minute setter-to-closer sync. They open on a newly booked lead, Sean, a 23-year-old firefighter with severe immobility, which Richard says is a copy-paste of a 28-year-old he closed weeks earlier, and he rehearses the consequence frame he intends to run. The setter then hands over a second lead, Bo Reid, who refused to book because he believes the call is just a closer trying to get him to commit, and asked for plan options by email. They discuss how the setter answered that text, how closers are described to leads, show rates against another closer, a prior no-show, and opening more calendar slots.
notable: Qualification override stated openly: 'the fact that he's 23 did make me question financial qualification a bit, but, you know, as Chris was saying earlier, he was such a good fit, I thought I'd let it slide, and either way, I think we'll get him through on the primal year.' ICP income screening waived at the setter stage with a cheaper tier as the fallback.
A lead who asked to see plan options in writing was told 'we don't have a standard menu of plans. It's all custom', while the company offer is fixed at $6,000/6mo and $9,000/12mo.

Closers are offered to leads as 'advisors'; the rep is relaxed about the label — 'if they know I'm a closer, can just tell I'm a closer, it doesn't matter' and 'you don't even need to say advisor anymore'.
The rep prefers a WhatsApp voice note over a text specifically because 'that builds so much more trust'.

No-show / loss handling: the setter is asked to call a prior no-show, Jeffrey, not to rebook but to learn the reason, and the rep pre-empts it himself — 'maybe he's like, well, Richard was too pushy. I would be surprised if that would be his reason'. The rep also calls that prospect 'a little of a weirdo'.
A team member named Chris is referenced who is not one of the three coded setters (KFS, KL, DH).

Counterpart identity rests on the file title: at 00:03:16 the rep says 'Just spoke to Kim and I'm speaking to him on Wednesday', which conflicts with Kim being the person on the call. Most likely transcription noise.
